messages:
alex: FYI — canary on the h100 dedicated pool spiked ~15-30% token latency after the CUDA/driver bump (14.1 -> 14.2). Seems sequence-length dependent; changes kick in around seq >= 384. Quick dump below from the profiler.
alex: ```profiling snippet
seq=512: attn_unroll_fallback     0.84ms  (prev: attn_opt_lmh 0.52ms)
seq=256: attn_opt_lmh             0.42ms
KV copy: small-batch memcpy ops up ~3x
Batching: avg batch size unchanged (1.9)
```

maria: Hmm. Do you have the kernel name switch logs? Could be autotuner re-ranking after driver exposes different perf counters. Any change to KV-cache hit ratio or memcpy pattern?

jin: We see same on two different canary nodes. Kernel pick changed from "attn_opt_lmh" -> "attn_unroll_fallback" for 384+ sequences in the autotuner logs. Autotuner score delta small but pushed ranking over threshold after driver patch.

alex: Pasted the autotuner excerpt: ```autotuner log
[2026-02-12T09:11:02Z] model=vicuna-13b seq=512 candidates=[attn_unroll_fallback:0.502, attn_opt_lmh:0.498] selected=attn_unroll_fallback
```

samir: Ops note: this pattern is consistent with a tiny throughput swing causing the deterministic selector to flip. We should either pin driver on canary or force deterministic kernel picks for now. Rolling everything back would be heavy.

maria: Also noticed increased small memcpy time — appears driver introduced a new memcpy kernel path that regresses tiny transfers. That would explain KV-copy spikes. Can try forcing batched KV copy to amortize overhead: runtime flag `kv_copy_strategy=batched` as a mitigation.

jin: I'm starting a quick bisect of autotuner scoring with the new driver vs old. Will run `make perf-suite` across seq 64/128/256/384/512/1024 and log kernel ranks. Adding AUTOTUNE_SEED=42 to get deterministic ordering while we debug.

alex: Proposed rollback plan (canary-first):
1) Pin driver back to 535.86 on the 6 canary h100 nodes
2) Deploy runtime patch to set `AUTOTUNE_MODE=fixed` or hard-pin the attn kernel for seq>=384 for 24h
3) Run perf suite and compare p95 token latency across seq buckets
4) If stable, roll to dedicated pool with gradual ramp.
Also open a bug with Nvidia w/ kernel timings + nvprof traces.

samir: I'll do the driver pin on canary now. Command I'll run: ```ansible-playbook -i canaries drivers/rollback.yml -e driver_version=535.86``` ETA ~ 20m. Will restart inference runtime gracefully (drain, restart, resume).

ops-bot: Scheduled: driver rollback on `canary-h100-{01..06}` at 2026-02-12T09:45Z. Will post completion status.

maria: While rollback goes, I'll kick off a perf job with `kv_copy_strategy=batched` and `AUTOTUNE_MODE=fixed` to see delta. If memcpy kernel is the culprit, batched strategy should recover most of the cost.

jin: After rollback + fixed-autotune test, I'll also run a quick kernel microbench with cuda-memcpy small payloads to reproduce the memcpy regression. If reproducible, we file detailed repro to Nvidia with a minimal cuMemcpy case.

alex: Sounds good. Thanks all. Keep thread updated with timings before/after. If rollback doesn't help, we'll escalate rollback to the dedicated pool and open a postmortem template. :thumbsup:

samir: rollback complete on canaries. Early telemetry shows token p95 back down ~16% to baseline. I'll keep monitoring for 1h then propose next steps.

perfbot: CI perf-suite run queued: run-id=perf-20260212-01, matrices=seq[64,128,256,384,512,1024], autotune=fixed+batched_kv. Results will be pushed to /perf-runs/2026-02-12/1869999999.json
